newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina denies labor reform promises to business.
newsitem.headline: Argentina denies labor reform promises to business.

text.p: Argentina's Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa denied Friday the government has promised business leaders it will change the preliminary agreement it has reached with unions on labor market reforms.

"Rather than promising anything, we exhaustively explained the terms of the deal with the CGT" during a meeting between government officials and members of the Group of Eight major business lobbies Thursday, Figueroa was quoted as saying by state news agency Telam.

After months of disagreement, Argentina's government and the CGT reached a preliminary agreement on labor reform a week ago but the deal needs approval from the Group of Eight to go ahead. The deal could lead unions to drop plans of staging a general strike this month.

The details of the accord have not yet been announced but the government has been pushing to swap termination payments for unemployment insurance and allow workers to make salary and contract agreements directly with employers with no centralized union intervention.

Figueroa denied, however, that the government had promised business leaders that there would be changes to hours worked, holidays, overtime pay and the way in which the annual bonus of an extra month's salary is paid.
"We did not even touch upon these issues, although surely we will do so in coming talks," he said.

The government argues that making the labor market more flexible is crucial to reducing employer costs that prevent hiring. That is key to decreasing the near-record unemployment rate of 17.3 percent, it argues.
